synopsis: Satellite positioning and inertial sensing provide the position and motion reference for other measurements, so reference accuracy sets the floor for warning-distance and stopping-distance accuracy [f12695, f12707]. The recommended ground truth combines surveyed targets, reference lidar with RTK-GNSS/INS for continuous distance and timing, and human-audited auto-labels; lidar’s blindness in dust requires a “truth unavailable” state [f100, f5197, f12613]. Reconstruction needs synchronised, calibrated sensor logs, and Para-Lane found RTK/INS trajectories alone insufficient for frame alignment, adding lidar mapping and camera-to-lidar registration [f3852, f4020]. Underground and GNSS-denied sites undermine RTK/INS-dependent reconstruction, so the booklet recommends retaining state-estimation inputs and solutions; Pretoria’s methodology uses GPS truth on the surface and lidar, cameras and radar underground [f4365, f4019, f1726]. Position and message paths are comparatively easy to emulate, but physical coverage, propagation, synchronisation and failure evidence remain necessary; NIOSH observed a brief 15 m GPS position shift during 2007 field work [f500, f502, f689]. Several tools offer GPS/GNSS and IMU models, but the research found no fidelity studies for GNSS/V2X proximity systems and no current public heavy off-road standard prescribing their laboratory-injection architecture, leaving model availability distinct from demonstrated validation adequacy [f8381, f8468, f8495, f8511, f4598, f5325].
